transcript: Hi welcome to Radical at Autoport International 2010. Here we are on our
gleaming white stand. We've got five cars here. First car you see this is arguably
one of the best-known Radicals. This is the actual car that gained the lap
record at the Nürburgring. This is an SR8 LM, LN standing for Le Mans. This has
a 2.8 litre engine which we make ourselves in-house with Powertech our
engine company and this car in August broke the lap record that we already had.
The record stood at 6 minutes 56 and we knocked that down to 6 minutes 48 in the
hands of Michael Burgess and so we are the outright production sports car lap
record holders around the ring.
Also
on the stand we have PR6. This is a Quaife Engineering sponsored car. Quaife manufacture
all our drive systems for us. In this car, which is a chain driven car, they make the
reversing differential for us. This is a clever device that allows the engine to drive
the car in reverse as well as forward. The PR6 is eligible for our Radical Clubman Cup
which we've now
called the Quaife Radical Clubman Cup. This is an eight round series that's run in the
UK for just motorcycle powered Radicals. I think there's about 20 races held at top UK
circuits. They're normally one day events with two sprints in the afternoon and I think
at a couple of events we've got double headers with four races. This car has a 1340cc Suzuki
engine. It's a very, very quick car.
And then over here, this is our SR3.
This is our most popular car.
We've manufactured over 500 of them to date.
The SR3 is eligible for our Radical UK Cup
and also our Europe-wide Radical European Masters,
which this year is sponsored by Shell Racing Solutions.
They're supplying all fuel and the lubricants for our series
and providing all the competitors with merchandise and jackets and that sort of thing.
This car can be raced in any of those championships,
including the Clubman's Cup.
Going over here, this is our low-cost model.
It's our SR4.
We've named this one the SR4 CZ.
CZ after Czechoslovakia,
because our Czechoslovakian distributor is selling these into the Eastern Bloc countries,
we are preparing a Radical Central and Eastern European Championship on SR4 models.
Our races will be in Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and Czech Republic.
And maybe also the countries like Croatia and Slovenia will take part.
It's a great idea.
It's another step for Radical taking what we're good at in the UK and Europe
and taking it to other parts of the world.
A lot of people in Eastern Croatia,
other countries are right now starting to spend their free time weekends on circuits
with their cars like Ferraris, Aston Martins, BMWs, M3s, etc., etc.
And they finally found out how expensive it is to make a motorsport on these large, big, heavy cars.
They also see that the Radicals are faster, cheaper, and it's a lot of fun because you are sitting in an open car
and it's always different.
It's not like Formula racing, but for much better money.
Also exciting for us for this year, we've started a hill climb series in Italy.
And this is a very, very popular car for that, fitted with a 1500 cc engine.
This is very competitive on the hills.
And we now have about 25 cars running in that series run by our distributor in Southern Italy.
So we're very pleased about that.
So this is our run.
We've got a range of petrol engine cars, ranging from the Superbike power engine,
which we were the first to develop that, over to our V8, which we manufacture ourselves.
Again, a Radical first.
And, of course, over to our electrical powered car.
We've always prided ourselves on being new and being the first.
This, I think, is a good example of that.
Who knows?
This may be the future of British motorsport.
And if it is, we want to be there leading the way.
A car that holds the lap record around the Nürburgring is 400 brake horsepower.
And that's exactly what this puts out.
So this is likely to be exciting.
It may not sound loud, but it's going to be exciting.
